title: Anonymous Sources and the Limits of Trust
text:
Journalists often rely on anonymous sources when disclosure would expose a person to genuine danger. The practice is defended as a means of revealing wrongdoing that would otherwise remain hidden. Yet anonymity also allows claims to circulate without accountability, since the reader cannot assess the motives or credibility of the speaker.

Careful reporters therefore attempt to corroborate anonymous claims with independent evidence and to describe the source's position in as much detail as possible. A phrase such as 'a senior official said' conveys authority while withholding identity, and readers should ask what that authority is based on. Transparency about sourcing is, in this sense, a form of respect for the audience.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, why do journalists rely on anonymous sources?
options: To avoid writing articles at all
When disclosure would expose a person to genuine danger
Because editors require it for every story
To increase the length of their reports

questions.text: What do careful reporters attempt to do with anonymous claims?
options: Remove all details about the source

questions.text: What does the passage imply about the phrase 'a senior official said'?
options: It reveals the official's identity completely
It conveys authority while withholding identity, so readers should question its basis
It shows that the reporter has no sources

questions.text: Why might transparency about sourcing be described as a form of respect for the audience?
options: It lets readers judge the credibility of the claims for themselves
It hides uncertainty from the reader

the obligation to answer for one's statements and actions

paragraph_translations: Jornalistas frequentemente recorrem a fontes anônimas quando a divulgação exporia uma pessoa a um perigo real. A prática é defendida como um meio de revelar irregularidades que, de outro modo, permaneceriam ocultas. No entanto, o anonimato também permite que afirmações circulem sem responsabilização, já que o leitor não consegue avaliar as motivações ou a credibilidade de quem fala.

Repórteres cuidadosos, por isso, tentam corroborar as afirmações anônimas com evidências independentes e descrever a posição da fonte com o máximo de detalhes possível. Uma expressão como «uma alta autoridade afirmou» transmite autoridade ao mesmo tempo que oculta a identidade, e os leitores devem perguntar em que se baseia essa autoridade. Nesse sentido, a transparência sobre as fontes é uma forma de respeito pelo público.
